claims.explanation: MG-132 is a proteasome inhibitor, so selectivity likely reflects dependence on proteasome-mediated degradation of specific substrates rather than PSMB1 mutation status. The most plausible sensitizing context is high NF-kB pathway activity, because proteasome inhibition blocks IkB degradation and NF-kB activation, and NF-kB is constitutively active in primitive AML and other tumor cells. TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines and is therefore not a strong selective feature; lineage and additional mutations such as PIK3CA, PTEN, or FBXW7 may modulate sensitivity but are less consistent.

features.basis: Proteasome inhibition blocks IkB degradation and NF-kB activation; NF-kB is constitutively active in primitive AML and other tumors
NF-kB pathway activity depends on proteasomal degradation of IkB; high RELA activity may increase dependence on proteasome function
HIF-1alpha is rapidly degraded by the ubiquitin-proteasome system under normoxia; proteasome inhibition stabilizes HIF-1alpha
VHL loss stabilizes HIF-1alpha and may increase dependence on proteasomal degradation pathways; VHL-mutant 786O is selectively killed
PIK3CA mutations appear enriched in several selectively killed lines (SNU840, HGC27, SNUC5, MKN1, KE39)
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling and may increase proteasome dependence; seen in 786O, UACC62, FTC133
FBXW7 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase; loss may alter ubiquitin-proteasome substrate degradation and sensitivity
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not a strong sensitizing feature and may be weakly protective
KRAS mutations appear in several least-affected lines (CL11, OV7, T3M4, SNU410) and may reduce proteasome dependence
BRAF mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant melanoma lines, but resistant lines IGR37 and K029AX are BRAF-mutant
CDKN2A mutations appear in several least-affected lines (MHHES1, K029AX, SNU1214)
ARID1A mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but resistant HEC265 and KU1919 are ARID1A-mutant
